A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DetPO work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DetPO experiments on Roboflow20-VL and LVIS Rare 50, including confidence-scoring ablations, error analyses, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original repeated-run, error-sampling, and multiclass evaluation results in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: Appendix J adds a multiclass inference adaptation that summarizes separately optimized class descriptions into one compact prompt. The original optimization and confidence-scoring procedures remain unchanged. The expanded validation-selection and visual-critique explanations in Section 3 already appeared in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Roboflow20-VL datasets and LVIS Rare 50 subset for few-shot object detection. The added analyses reuse existing coverage; single-class versus multiclass prompting changes the evaluation procedure rather than introducing new data or domains.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds GEPA to the reported comparisons against DetPO using Qwen3-VL-8B; v1's corresponding 8B results lacked this comparator. The original specialist detectors, GEPA, MIPROv2, and fine-tuning comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Tables 9–10 introduce controlled comparisons of random versus worst-error selection and single-class versus summarized multiclass inference for Qwen3-VL 8B and 30B. Existing benchmark metrics, shot settings, and documented training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices H–J substantially expand the diagnostic evidence by testing optimization stability, the value of selecting the worst errors, and whether DetPO's advantage persists under multiclass inference. These address important assumptions not tested by v1's retained confidence, shot-count, error, and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 adds a targeted Qwen3-VL-8B analysis with seeds 42–44, per-run scores, and mean ± standard deviation in Table 8. This newly documents three runs; it does not establish an increase from a previously specified run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New tables report 15.4 ± 0.1 overall mAP across three 8B runs; random sampling scores 15.6/19.6 versus worst-error sampling's 15.3/19.4 for 8B/30B. Multiclass DetPO scores 12.5/16.0 versus GEPA's 11.6/13.0. These are added comparisons, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C's mathematical definitions, error-score formulas, update rules, and validation-selection equations are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the new analyses introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about ineffective naive multimodal prompting and DetPO's benefits. Changing the abstract's '9.7%' to '9.7 mAP' clarifies the unit of the already reported absolute difference rather than establishing a new contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a medical-domain limitation and suggests that prompt optimization works best when base-model capability is neither weak nor saturated. It also interprets the small random-sampling advantage as within run variability, hypothesizes benefits of worst-error selection on larger training sets, and attributes multiclass degradation to prompt length.

D1.justification: Appendix J supplies the new multiclass summarization template, and the abstract redirects resource access to a project page while retaining the repository link in Appendix C. v2 removes the sentence identifying LLaMAFactory for Qwen fine-tuning. Original implementation settings and prompt templates otherwise remain.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit positioning argument contrasting DetPO's visual error feedback with GEPA's purported numeric-only feedback. The bibliography removes the MMDetection and LLaMAFactory references; the remaining cited works are retained after renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the method introduction, expands refinement and validation explanations, revises captions, and extends the limitations discussion. The overall narrative, section sequence, and most existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a pipeline diagram as Figure 2 and Tables 8–10, relocates existing displays, reorders comparison rows, and adjusts table emphasis and labels. All original figure images are retained unchanged, so the visual revision is additive and localized.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–10 add useful stability and design checks, including a more comparable multiclass evaluation against GEPA, while the new limitations discussion better qualifies applicability. These strengthen the retained evidence. The gain is limited by narrow seed coverage and the new numeric-only characterization of GEPA, which oversimplifies the structured feedback documented in Appendix B.
